text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past interactions as continuing interest in broadly related products or content, with insufficient attention to immediate purpose and recent context.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they continue a recognizable recent artist, musical style, story tone, or specific practical task.",
    "Complementary accessories and supplies appeal when they support existing equipment or add a useful capability."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with stronger matches despite requiring an unsupported project, device, listening mood, or viewing preference.",
    "Similar products are treated as plausible next purchases even when they duplicate an existing function, require unconfirmed compatibility, or offer an unsuitable quantity.",
    "Older seasonal or secondary interests receive more emphasis than users' current task or most recent content preference."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category, ecosystem, genre, and workshop associations substitute for a specific reason to choose an item.",
    "Past ownership or interaction is treated as evidence of demand for additional similar products or content."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent interactions help distinguish current intent from older, occasional, or secondary interests.",
    "Practical relevance depends on exact compatibility, application, quantity, and whether an item adds value beyond what the user already owns.",
    "Content choices depend on specific artist, tone, melody, atmosphere, and style rather than broad genre membership alone."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The top recommendations too often offer broad relatedness without a sufficiently specific connection to what the user would choose now.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked items users select with an explicit connection to a recent interaction or current task.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to duplication, incompatible specifications, unsuitable quantities, or unsupported project assumptions.",
    "The frequency with which users prefer a lower-ranked specific match over a higher-ranked item connected only by category, ecosystem, or genre.",
    "The proportion of judgments limited by unidentified content, tracked separately from explicit preference mismatches."
  ]
}
